"""tb -- the one way a device-testing session reaches a testbox (Ask-CK decision D6, 2026-10-09).

    tools/tb <action> <box> [args...]          run from the repo root (claude/device-testing/)

The action comes FIRST so each allow rule is anchored at the start of the command. Every ssh step bench-runner and the /test-mode sentinel take goes through ONE action here, so a
settings file can allow each action with one narrow rule (`Bash(tools/tb ckcon *)`) instead
of matching free-form `SSH_AUTH_SOCK=... ssh tbNNN '...'` strings. The wrapper sets
SSH_AUTH_SOCK itself (the keyring agent, TESTBOX-ACCESS.md §0), validates every argument, and
quotes everything it sends. It runs the step locally when the host IS <box>.

Login secrets: CK_USER / CK_PASSWORD and the per-console CK_USER_U<N> / CK_PASSWORD_U<N>
are forwarded to the box over STDIN and exported there before the tool runs -- never on the
remote command line, which `ps` shows to every other user on a shared box (2026-10-21).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""peek.py <tty> <baud> <transcript>: bare CR, report the prompt tail (the pre-run console
gate: is the unit at login:, '>', '#', a (config) mode, or silent?). Sends one CR and does
not log in. <tty> is the unit's console device on the testbox you run it on; <transcript>
is a path you choose (appended). The stty -hupcl is the IE520 DTR-drop/BREAK workaround
(see console.py); harmless on other AW+ products."""
import sys, os, time
USAGE = "usage: peek.py <tty> <baud> <transcript>"
if len(sys.argv) != 4 or sys.argv[1] in ("-h", "--help"):
    print(USAGE); sys.exit(0 if sys.argv[1:2] in (["-h"], ["--help"]) else 2)
try:
    tty, baud, tr = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3]
except ValueError as e:
    print(USAGE); print("bad argument: %s" % e); sys.exit(2)
import serial
os.system('stty -F {} -hupcl 2>/dev/null'.format(os.path.realpath(tty)))
s = serial.Serial(tty, baud, timeout=0.2)
t = open(tr, 'a', errors='replace'); t.write('\n===== peek {} {} =====\n'.format(tty, time.strftime('%F %T')))
time.sleep(0.3); s.read(8192)
s.write(b'\r'); buf=b''; t0=time.time()
while time.time()-t0 < 3.0:
    b = s.read(4096)
    if b: buf += b
t.write(buf.decode(errors='replace')); t.close(); s.close()
tail = buf.decode(errors='replace').replace('\r','').strip().splitlines()

## What a bench writes

Only what the framework already reads: `[switch]`, `[stack]`, `[portlink]` (plus power and
consoles as usual). **`[misc]` is not read by the frame or the preflight.** A bench that wants
to host a test cables it and declares the cable:

```ini
[switch]
swi_a = /dev/u2          ; the DUT slot (or a member of the DUT stack)
swi_e = /dev/u1          ; a partner — any name, it is a partner because of the cable below

[stack]
stk_a = swi_a, swi_b, swi_c, swi_d

[portlink]
tb-swi_c    = eth1-port3.0.2         ; testbox <-> DUT (a stack member)
swi_a-swi_e = port1.0.2-port1.0.2    ; DUT (member) <-> partner
swi_d-swi_e = port4.0.2-port1.0.4    ; a second DUT <-> partner cable
```

## The roles, and how `init()` binds them

`_detect_links()` (`routers/pytest_create.py`) decides from the case wording and the slice-C
`claim`s **how many links of which media the case needs** — a role set. The frame then binds
one link per role, discovered at run time:

text: The tester agent ran a read-only `fwcheck.py` that confirmed the framework's Setup.py API, then read the AWPTCM-T44187 IPv6 library helpers. No device output yet.

The PyTest Creator's last feedback on this case was its third review of `ssh_ipv6.py` (16 Sep, 22:41 UTC), followed by an automatic fix pass before the script was saved. That review raised 19 findings: 6 high, 11 medium, 2 low. I checked each one against the script we're validating now: 15 are fixed, 3 are still open, and 1 was handled differently than suggested.

**Still open, and probably the errors you're seeing:**

1. **Most cases connect to an IPv6 address the DUT doesn't have.** The suite's setup puts address index **10** on the DUT, but almost every case connects to index **2**. Thirteen TestCases (8, 10–13, 15–20, 25, 26) never add index 2 themselves, and the cases that do add it remove it again at the end. So those 13 connect to an address that isn't there. The deny-user, wrong-password and unknown-user checks would then "pass" because nothing answers, not because the DUT refused the login. The review flagged this; the fix pass didn't touch it.
2. **Hardcoded `manager`/`friend` logins.** TestCase_4 (loopback SSH), TestCase_18 (the sessions it terminates) and TestCase_22 (the check that the DUT still accepts new sessions) log in with an account the script never creates. If the 4050 doesn't have that login, these fail because the credentials are wrong, not because SSH is faulty. In TestCase_18 the connect isn't wrapped in error handling, so the case crashes with an exception instead of recording a FAIL.
3. **Step numbers are shifted by one.** TestCase_n logs "STEP n" but carries out step n+1 of the step list the PyTest Creator built. Step 1 there is the base setup and its `show running-config` check; it runs inside the suite setup and never gets a pass/fail.

**Handled differently than suggested:** for TestCase_4's loopback branch, the review wanted the framework's not-applicable result. The script now logs "not-applicable" without recording a PASS, which removes the false green the review objected to.

**Fixed:** the other 15. These include the address removal in TestCase_1, the output comparison in TestCase_6, the deny-user verdict, the refused-or-queued check for the extra session, the dead "unexpected" branch in TestCase_19, the client source address check, the after-restart login verdict, and the memory-leak check.

The PyTest Creator's last feedback on this case was its third review of `ssh_ipv6.py` (16 Sep, 22:41 UTC), followed by an automatic fix pass before the script was saved. **Still open, and probably the errors you're seeing:**

1. **Most cases connect to an IPv6 address the DUT doesn't have.** The suite's setup puts address index **10** on the DUT, but almost every case connects to index **2**. Thirteen TestCases (8, 10–13, 15–20, 25, 26) never add index 2 themselves, and the cases that do add it remove it again at the end. So those 13 connect to an address that isn't there. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ckcon.py <tty> <baud> <transcript> [--stop-on-error] CMD [CMD ...]

command and its output, and (with --stop-on-error) stop at the first "% " line.

sent only when a login prompt is showing, nothing else is sent until a prompt is seen,

you choose. Env: CKTO = per-command timeout s (default 90); CK_USER / CK_PASSWORD =
login credentials (default manager / friend).

about every 0.5 s (plus its own run time) until its output matches <regex> (re.M) or <s>
seconds pass, then prints MATCHED/TIMED OUT with the elapsed time and the last output; with

"""logout.py <tty> <baud> <transcript>: shared-box close-out. CR; only if an exec prompt
('name#' or 'name>') comes back, send `exit`; report the tail. Never types at login:/Password:."""
import os, re, sys, time, serial
tty, baud, tr = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3]
os.system('stty -F {} -hupcl 2>/dev/null'.format(os.path.realpath(tty)))

def rd(sec):
    b = b''; t0 = time.time()
    while time.time() - t0 < sec:
        x = s.read(4096)
        if x: b += x
    d = b.decode(errors='replace'); t.write(d); return d
rd(0.3); s.write(b'\r'); out = rd(2.0)
tail = out.replace('\r', '').strip().splitlines()[-1:] or ['']

else:
    print('%s: at %r, nothing sent' % (tty, tail[0]))
t.close(); s.close()
EOF

(one of the three human-owned non-repo directories under `claude/`). **3437 markdown
pages**, one per CLI command, each with:

- an Overview and the `no` variant
- a **Syntax** block
- the **Mode** it is valid in (this is the bit that keeps being the problem)
- a **Platform table** and links to family pages

([[grep-shim-honors-gitignore]]).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Look up AlliedWare Plus CLI syntax + real sample output from ck.db.

The retrieval half of the CLI-grounding work: `harvest_cli_docs.py` fills the tables,
this reads them. Importable (the generator injects `prompt_block()` output into the
generate prompt) and runnable (spot-check a command by hand).

Grounding matters because every model in the Part 2B matrix — Opus included — invented a
`speed=1000`/`state=up` output schema the switch never prints. Real output is
`current duplex full, current speed 1000, current polarity mdix`.

NOT a validity oracle: cross-command physical constraints are absent from the source

  python3 ask-ck/frontend/ck-main/current/pytest-creator/cli_lookup.py --product x930 duplex

  python3 ask-ck/frontend/ck-main/current/pytest-creator/cli_lookup.py --prompt-block "show interface,speed,duplex"

excerpt:
### `cfg.py`
Config and show driver for chatty consoles. Each command completes on the prompt after its echo,
so streams of port-state lines don't stall it. `YN:` commands are answered `y`. It always leaves
the console at exec with `terminal no monitor`.
- **Run:** `cfg.py <tty> <baud> <transcript> [YN:]CMD [[YN:]CMD ...]`
- **Where:** testbox; **needs:** pyserial
- **Imports:** console, awlogin
- **Exit codes:**
  - 2: CLI error;
  - 3: unexpected (y/n);
  - 5: no prompt within 90 s;
  - 6: an expected (y/n) did not appear;
  - 7: no privileged prompt.
- **Status:** verified 2026-10-02 on tb470, IE520 standalone (u3), read-only (`show clock`; the YN: path not exercised)

### `qmark.py`
Read-only CLI help probe. It types `PREFIX ?` with no CR, prints the completions offered, then
clears the line with Ctrl-U. A self-test first proves that nothing gets executed. Never send
`<cmd> ?` through a CR driver instead, because that executes the command (memory
`never-send-cli-help-through-a-cr-driver`).

**Run 2 rebooted both the 4050 and the x230, despite your "no restarts" constraint.** I assumed a run set up with no PDU couldn't restart anything, and that was wrong. Here's what happened:

1. TestCase_1 passed all of its own checks, but its tear_down left SSH off (`no service ssh`).
2. The framework compared the config against the starting point, found the difference, and logged "Setup is no longer reliable – all devices will be rebooted".
3. Without a PDU, it rebooted both units over the CLI at 16:03:17.
4. The tester killed the run at about 16:05, but the reboots were already under way.

**I've stopped the repair loop.** Any later TestCase that fails would reboot both units again. The only way to prevent that is to switch off the framework's restart, and STANDING-ORDERS §6 forbids that. So the case is BLOCKED and there will be no run 3.

**The tester is now finishing up:**
- waiting for both units to come back on `tb470-bench.cfg`;
- taking the health read after the run;
- restoring the 4050's original SSH and vlan1 settings and checking them against the pre-run config;
- writing the run 2 log;
- logging out of the consoles.

When it reports back, I'll record the result, run `/create-logs --auto` and close the campaign.

**Two decisions for you:**
- **A re-run.** This needs either "no restarts" lifted, or your ruling that the framework's restart may be switched off for this one campaign; STANDING-ORDERS §6 currently forbids that. The fixes made so far (R1–R9, plus the SSH tear_down fix) stay in the work copy for the next attempt.
- **The standing orders.** STANDING-ORDERS §1 says a session with no PDU power-cycles nothing. That's true of the PDU, but the framework can still reboot units over the CLI. Correcting that is the bench owner's call. It's recorded in the queue (commit `cab73d7`).
